topic: K1 prove IPW-SVD attains pointwise normalized max-row loss b_nm=K r^(3/2)mu q^(-1/2)sqrt(1/n+n/m^2) under recorded predictable masks. K2 match it by an adaptive-mask minimax lower bound. K3 prove blind row scaling is first-order valid iff restricted propensity drift rho<=b_nm. K4 keep b_nm separate and inflate simultaneous stochastic radii by sqrt(log |G_n|) for predeclared dense families |G_n|<=n^kappa. Include the rank-one .25/.75 Markov-mask witness and HeartSteps II consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Recorded propensities make IPW entry errors conditionally mean zero, so matrix Freedman concentration plus leave-one-row perturbation may recover the independent-mask rowwise scale. A constant-q subclass supplies a legal lower-bound packing. Expanding blind self-normalization should expose drift-correlated first-order bias. The Markov witness permits exact conditional calculations. Polynomial query families require a separate entropy multiplier; it cannot be hidden inside b_nm. Random denominator remainders and the iff threshold remain unchecked. A constant-propensity submodel also shows adaptivity cannot improve the minimax converse, but sharp constants remain open here. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Obtain martingale-sharp rowwise singular-vector perturbation, control adaptive self-normalized denominators, match the lower bound, and prove necessity and sufficiency of the drift threshold while separating simultaneous-query entropy. EARLY KILL TEST: Expand bias and variance exactly in the rank-one Markov witness. Stop if bias exceeds b_nm when rho<=b_nm, or if martingale concentration or sqrt(log |G_n|) inflation invalidates the stated pointwise benchmark.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether recorded-propensity IPW-SVD retains the independent-mask pointwise normalized max-row rate b_nm = K r^(3/2) mu q^(-1/2) sqrt(1/n + n/m^2) under history-predictable masks.

source_refs.author: Changxiao Cai, Gen Li, Yuejie Chi, H. Vincent Poor, Yuxin Chen

the hard parts are the uniform perturbation bound for deterministic staggered masks

open_problems.why_unsolved: The independent-mask ell_2,infinity argument uses leave-one-out decoupling, whereas deleting one row under a predictable design can change later mask probabilities and destroy the needed independence. Tropp controls the operator norm of the conditionally centered IPW martingale but not its rowwise singular-vector perturbation; Han, Sun, and Zhang handle adaptivity with online SGD rather than IPW-SVD. The prior panel runs likewise stop at serial-dependence and deterministic-mask perturbation boundaries. A proof must replace the first decoupling step by a filtration-preserving leave-one-row construction and bound random IPW denominators below b_nm; the targeted scan found no paper joining these components.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A nonasymptotic high-probability theorem, uniform over a stated predictable-propensity and incoherent low-rank class, proving normalized max-row loss at most C b_nm for IPW-SVD with a martingale-compatible leave-one-row expansion and an o(b_nm) adaptive-denominator remainder.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing explains why global matrix error is insufficient and makes rowwise subspace accuracy the operative statistical target.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: partial noisy matrix observations -> global error can conceal heterogeneous row failure -> ell_2,infinity control becomes the target -> recover that target under recorded predictable masks

method_exemplars.technique: Diagonal-deleted Gram spectral estimation and leave-one-out perturbation separating spectral error from rowwise incoherence terms.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves the same ell_2,infinity object under independent partial observations; row deletion and decoupling are precisely the proof steps that must become filtration preserving.

method_exemplars.technique: Matrix Laplace-transform proof of Freedman concentration through predictable quadratic variation and bounded martingale increments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Recorded-propensity IPW entry errors are conditionally centered, so Hermitian dilation turns their spectral perturbation into the matrix-martingale object this result controls.

method_exemplars.technique: Supermartingale localization of low-rank stochastic-gradient iterates followed by online double debiasing and a martingale CLT.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its filtration bookkeeping is the closest adaptive low-rank template, although the destination requires a spectral max-row rather than online-SGD expansion.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the minimax normalized max-row risk over predictable adaptive masks and whether a constant-propensity submodel already forces the b_nm rate for every history-adaptive estimator.

source_refs.claim: The independent partial-observation model has matching ell_2,infinity minimax lower bounds in its noise parameters.
source_refs.author: Changxiao Cai, Gen Li, Yuejie Chi, H. Vincent Poor, Yuxin Chen

source_refs.author: Jiayi Wang, Raymond K. W. Wong, Xiaojun Mao, Kwun Chuen Gary Chan

source_refs.excerpt: This is a nonconstant, non-random-mask staggered witness for the below-threshold side
Construct Choi--Yuan-legal triangular arrays whose standardized nonlinear remainder attains the Delta_CY scale

open_problems.why_unsolved: Published sharp rowwise and heterogeneous-missingness converses use fixed or independent sampling laws, while adaptive low-rank papers focus on regret, convergence, or pointwise inference. The archived CausalSmith witnesses are single nonidentification or nonlinear-remainder paths, not noisy many-hypothesis packings. The first new proof step is to construct an incoherent rank-r packing separated in normalized max-row loss and compute its sequential likelihood conditional on the mask filtration. A constant-q mask is a legal submodel and should prevent adaptivity from lowering worst-case risk, but Frobenius or entrywise bounds do not automatically yield the exact rectangular geometry, r^(3/2) mu factor, q dependence, or sharp constants in b_nm.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A Le Cam, Assouad, or Fano theorem proving inf_hatM sup_(M,pi predictable) E[L_max-row(hatM,M)] >= c b_nm on the same class as the IPW-SVD upper bound, via an explicit constant-q low-rank packing and a regime statement matching the upper rate.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates the move beyond uniform sampling and treats a matching information lower bound as essential to the rate claim.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: uniform missingness is unrealistic -> weighting accommodates heterogeneous observation rates -> upper guarantees need an information benchmark -> characterize worst-case risk after enlarging masks to predictable adaptive laws

method_exemplars.technique: Separated incoherent low-rank subspace alternatives combined with information inequalities for an ell_2,infinity minimax converse.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its loss geometry is closest to normalized max-row error; embedding its alternatives into the constant-q predictable-mask submodel transfers the information obstruction.

method_exemplars.technique: Minimax reduction over heterogeneous observation probabilities paired with a weighting estimator whose risk exposes probability dependence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It shows how missingness heterogeneity enters both sides of a rate theorem; the destination replaces its fixed law by a predictable class while retaining a fixed-propensity hard subset.

method_exemplars.technique: Local low-rank perturbations and conditional information calculations establishing optimality for noisy matrix-completion inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its local alternatives help distinguish a rate-only max-row converse from a sharper constant-level statement in the adaptive experiment.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize blind row self-normalization under predictable masks by proving that it has the same first-order b_nm rowwise guarantee as recorded-propensity IPW if and only if restricted propensity drift rho is at most order b_nm.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Khan and Ugander's normalization expansion assumes independent indicators, whereas adaptive-experiment work keeps recorded predictable propensities and the prior CausalSmith result validates same-path normalization only after separating the scale-selecting information from the leading numerator. Blind row scaling violates that separation: its denominator and singular-vector numerator are driven by the same mask path, creating a drift-correlated first-order term plus nonlinear denominator remainders. Scalar adaptive-IPW and fixed-law low-rank arguments therefore do not give an iff boundary at b_nm. Necessity needs an exact signed calculation on the rank-one 0.25/0.75 Markov mask, while sufficiency needs uniform self-normalized denominator control.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An iff theorem showing blind row scaling has uniform O_P(b_nm) normalized max-row loss exactly when rho <= C b_nm, based on an expansion into the recorded-IPW influence term plus an explicit drift-bias functional and o_P(b_nm) remainder, with a rank-one 0.25/0.75 Markov-mask counterexample proving failure beyond the threshold.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing makes normalization a statistical design choice and explicitly isolates dependence among observation indicators as the next boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: inverse weighting is unbiased but noisy -> data-adaptive normalization can improve precision -> dependence changes numerator-denominator covariance -> locate the sharp drift boundary for blind row normalization under predictable masks

method_exemplars.technique: Joint Taylor expansion of an IPW numerator and data-dependent affine denominator, interpreted through a control-variate representation with variance comparison.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired threshold is governed by the same numerator-denominator covariance, but the proof must replace independent indicators with predictable Markov-dependent row masks.

method_exemplars.technique: Predictable weighting of adaptive AIPW martingale increments to stabilize conditional variance, followed by a martingale CLT and studentization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the filtration-aware recorded-propensity expansion against which discarding propensities through blind row scaling must be compared.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate a structured propensity matrix and propagate inverse-probability-weight error through low-rank completion risk bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest low-rank propensity-aware analysis; the destination asks when a row total can replace its entrywise propensity correction to first order.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Xia and Yuan give fixed-linear-form limits, Ma et al. give matrix-specific simultaneous inference under modeled missingness, and Belloni and Oliveira give maxima theory for martingales without a nonlinear spectral remainder. The prior panel run asks for scalar-versus-simultaneous width accounting, while the accepted finite-M argument uses independent local cells rather than predictable low-rank scores. The missing first step is a martingale linear representation uniform over dense G_n after rowwise SVD, followed by feasible covariance and anti-concentration control when contrasts can be nearly collinear. The entropy cost belongs to the maximum of the stochastic linear terms; absorbing sqrt(log |G_n|) into b_nm would erase the distinct pointwise benchmark.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform Gaussian-approximation or multiplier-bootstrap theorem for max_(g in G_n) |studentized(g(hatM-M))| with |G_n| <= n^kappa, yielding honest simultaneous bands of radius C b_nm sqrt(log |G_n|) together with a separate pointwise theorem at radius C b_nm and an explicit uniform spectral-remainder condition.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative moves from low-rank recovery to coordinatewise distribution theory and then to a clearly separate simultaneous-inference layer.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: completion estimates latent low-rank structure -> scientific use requires uncertainty quantification -> many contrasts are queried together -> build simultaneous inference for dense causal contrasts under predictable masks

method_exemplars.technique: Double-sample debiasing, projection onto estimated singular spaces, and a first-order linear representation for arbitrary matrix linear forms.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each member of G_n is such a linear form; the destination must make the representation and its remainder uniform over a polynomial family under martingale sampling.

method_exemplars.technique: Gaussian coupling, anti-concentration, and multiplier bootstrap for the coordinatewise maximum of a high-dimensional martingale.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After uniform spectral linearization, the vector of dense contrast errors is a high-dimensional martingale and this machinery produces the separate sqrt(log |G_n|) maximum scale.

method_exemplars.technique: Matrix-completion linearization with feasible covariance estimation and multiplier-bootstrap simultaneous testing.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest matrix-specific simultaneous construction; predictable masks replace its observation model and dense causal contrasts replace coefficient coordinates.

literature_map:
Cai, Li, Chi, Poor, and Chen (2021, Annals of Statistics) give the closest independent-mask ell_2,infinity spectral benchmark and matching minimax noise dependence.
Chen, Fan, Ma, and Yan (2019, PNAS) establish debiased entry/factor inference and statistical optimality for noisy matrix completion under standard random sampling.
Xia and Yuan (2021, JRSSB) extend matrix-completion inference to fixed general linear forms through debiasing and singular-space projection.
Mao, Wong, and Chen (2021, Statistica Sinica) estimate a structured propensity matrix and use IPW completion, but their mechanism is nonsequential.
Wang, Wong, Mao, and Chan (2021, ICML) replace propensity modeling by balancing weights and prove a heterogeneous-missingness minimax lower bound.
Bhattacharya and Chatterjee (2022, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory) study data-dependent missingness probabilities, underscoring the limits of fixed Bernoulli sampling.
Choi and Yuan (2024, JASA) develop inference for MNAR matrix completion in causal panels, but not predictable masks or normalized max-row rates.
Krishnamurthy and Singh (2013, NeurIPS) and Balcan and Zhang (2016) study actively chosen samples for completion, with objectives distinct from passive recorded-propensity IPW-SVD.
Han, Sun, and Zhang (2025, Annals of Statistics) provide the closest adaptive low-rank inference result, using online SGD and double debiasing.
Tropp (2011, ECP) supplies matrix Freedman concentration; the missing bridge is martingale-sharp leave-one-row singular-vector perturbation.
Khan and Ugander (2023, Journal of Causal Inference) analyze adaptive normalization under independent indicators and explicitly flag dependent indicators as a future direction.
Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey (2021, PNAS) show why adaptive collection complicates ordinary IPW and use predictable variance-stabilizing weights.
Belloni and Oliveira (2018) provide high-dimensional martingale Gaussian coupling and bootstrap machinery for polynomial query families.
Ma, Niu, Zhang, and Zhu (2025, JASA) provide matrix-specific multiplier-bootstrap simultaneous inference under covariate-modeled missingness.
Spruijt-Metz et al. (2022, IJERPH) document that HeartSteps II saves personalized randomization probabilities, making recorded-versus-blind normalization operationally relevant.
